diagnosis_plan.title: Exclude frozen backbone parameters from the optimizer
diagnosis_plan.description: In train.py, change optimizer construction from `torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-4)` to `torch.optim.AdamW(model.head.parameters(), lr=1e-4)` so that only the head parameters (intended trainable set) receive AdamW state. The backbone is already in eval() and has requires_grad=True unintentionally; restricting the optimizer to the head eliminates the 8.6 GB of optimizer_state (two fp32 moment buffers per backbone parameter) and the associated temporary allocations during the AdamW step.
diagnosis_plan.risk: Low. The code comment states the intended contract is to train only the head. The change aligns the optimizer with that contract and does not alter forward/backward math for the head. The backbone remains in eval() and its parameters stay frozen.

diagnosis_plan.title: Enable gradient accumulation to reduce peak activations and temporaries
diagnosis_plan.description: Introduce gradient accumulation in train.py: process micro-batches (e.g., split batch=8 into 4 micro-batches of 2), call loss.backward() for each without optimizer.step(), then call optimizer.step() once per effective batch. This reduces the live activation working set and temporary buffers at any one time because each micro-batch's forward/backward frees its tensors before the next. The policy allow_batch_grad_accum=true permits this change.
diagnosis_plan.risk: Medium. Requires verifying that the effective batch size, loss reduction (mean vs sum), and optimizer update boundary remain mathematically equivalent. The current script uses a single batch of 8; micro-batch size and accumulation steps must be chosen so that the number of samples per optimizer update and the loss scaling are preserved.

diagnosis_plan.title: Exclude frozen backbone parameters from optimizer
diagnosis_plan.description: Change optimizer construction to only include model.head.parameters() instead of model.parameters(). The backbone is frozen (eval() and no_grad) but its parameters were being passed to AdamW, causing optimizer state (moments) to be allocated for them. This is supported by stk_b488709a683c5eb8 showing 4.3 GB optimizer_state and source line 108. The previous verification round 1 attempted this but failed numerical acceptance because loss comparison used different effective batch/objective (unknown_checks). This fix preserves mathematics if head-only training is the intended objective.
diagnosis_plan.risk: Changes which parameters receive optimizer updates; must confirm head-only training is the intended objective. Previous attempt failed numerical acceptance due to unverified loss comparability (different inputs/effective batch/objective not established).

diagnosis_plan.title: Add torch.no_grad() context for backbone forward
diagnosis_plan.description: Wrap the backbone forward call in torch.no_grad() to prevent autograd from saving activations for the frozen backbone. In train.py line 91, the forward is 'return self.head(self.backbone(x))'. Since backbone is in eval() and intended frozen, its activations should not be retained for backward. This targets the activations category (stk_523ffc8c089e3758, stk_5ae507471d8ce8a7) and may reduce temporaries in backward. Source shows backbone.eval() but no no_grad guard.
diagnosis_plan.risk: Low; ensures no gradients computed for backbone. Must verify head still receives gradients.

diagnosis_plan.title: Set requires_grad=False on backbone parameters
diagnosis_plan.description: Explicitly set requires_grad=False for all backbone parameters after model construction. This prevents them from being included in model.parameters() (which filters by requires_grad) and ensures no gradient buffers are allocated. Combined with fix1, provides defense in depth. Source line 107 comment confirms 'backbone requires_grad was never disabled'.
diagnosis_plan.risk: None; makes freezing explicit. May allow optimizer to automatically exclude them even if model.parameters() used.

diagnosis_plan.title: Reduce micro-batch size and increase gradient accumulation steps

diagnosis_plan.risk: Significant throughput regression (~20-30%) due to recomputation. Must verify loss equivalence.
